target_architecture: Target Architecture v1.0 (Core / Packs / Plugins / Control Plane / Runtime / Gateways)
method: 16 parallel read-only domain auditors + a completeness critic, plus orchestrator verification of the 12 contracts and the CI configuration. Every non-MISSING record carries file:line, symbol, service, table, route or test evidence.

records.capability: Central LLM gateway client (chat completions)
records.evidence: backend/services/llm.py:33 `CHAT_URL = f"{LLM_BASE_URL.rstrip('/')}/chat/completions"`; API surface `complete()` (:188), `complete_raw()` (:221), `acomplete()` (:257), `acomplete_raw()` (:272), `astream()` (:282); typed errors `LLMError` (:44), `LLMTimeoutError` (:48), `LLMGatewayError` (:57), `LLMEmptyResponseError` (:62); pooled `get_client()` (:238). Imported by 12 modules: backend/documents.py:21, backend/evals/runner.py:369, backend/ingest.py:153, backend/knowledge_graph/extractor.py:20, backend/knowledge_graph/retrieval/resolver.py:22, backend/mail_intel.py:17, backend/main.py:29, backend/routes/observability_explorer.py:230, integrations/document_handler.py:7, memory/long_term.py:80, memory/query_rewriter.py:23, memory/summarizer.py:1
records.current_implementation: Thin httpx client over the LiteLLM OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions route, model name defaulted from LLM_MODEL in build_payload() (llm.py:159), Qwen3 reasoning disabled via chat_template_kwargs NO_THINK (llm.py:71).
records.gap: No fallback, no retry, and no embeddings method on the gateway; a single httpx.post per call (llm.py:205). Resilience is entirely delegated to LiteLLM config that is not in the repo.
records.architectural_risk: Low — this is the intended target component and is correctly used by the majority of call sites.

records.capability: LiteLLM proxy model registry (model_list / routing / fallbacks / keys)
records.target_requirement: Versioned model registry backing the gateway
records.evidence: No file in the repo declares `model_list`, `litellm_settings` or `master_key`: `grep -rln -E "model_list|litellm_settings|master_key" --include=*.yaml --include=*.yml --include=*.json` returns nothing (excluding .venv/node_modules). `find . -maxdepth 3 -name "*litellm*" -o -name "*.yaml"` returns only `./.env.bak.pre-litellm`. deploy/ contains only aganeti-api.service and aria-whisper.service. requirements.txt has no `litellm` entry.
records.current_implementation: Configured out-of-band on the host; the repo only carries the alias strings that reference it.
records.gap: The model names the code depends on — `qwen-fast` (settings.py:43), `qwen-vl` (settings.py:47), `qwen-extract` (settings.py:230) — are LiteLLM model_list aliases that exist only on the deployed host. Nothing in version control proves qwen-vl or qwen-extract are registered, and per-route timeouts, retries and fallbacks referenced in backend/services/llm.py:7 and :179 are unreviewable.
records.architectural_risk: The single most load-bearing config in the domain is unversioned. A gateway rebuild loses routing, keys and fallbacks with no repo artifact to restore from; KG_EXTRACT_MODEL=qwen-extract silently 404s if the alias is absent.

records.capability: Second parallel model gateway (orchestrator router)
records.evidence: Stack A: backend/services/llm.py (httpx, `CHAT_URL` :33, pooled `get_client()` :238). Stack B: backend/orchestrator/llm.py:8 `from . import router` -> backend/orchestrator/router.py:21 `from openai import AsyncOpenAI`, own client cache `_clients: dict[str, AsyncOpenAI]` (router.py:77), own registry `MODELS` (router.py:35-48), own planner `plan()` (router.py:100-122), own fallback loop `complete()` (router.py:155-178), own cost logging `_log()` (router.py:135-144). Stack B consumers: backend/orchestrator/graph.py:21,64 `msg = await llm.chat(...)`; backend/chat/memory.py:373-374; evals/tool_calling_eval.py:73,79,87 `router.complete(...)`.
records.current_implementation: Both stacks ultimately address LLM_BASE_URL for local models (router.py:36-47 all set base_url=LLM_BASE_URL), so local traffic does reach LiteLLM — but through two different clients with two different contracts.
records.gap: Two independent inference paths with divergent behaviour: Stack A strips <think> via ThinkFilter/strip_think (llm.py:86,100), Stack B does not; Stack B logs kind='llm_call' cost events, Stack A logs none; Stack B has chain fallback, Stack A has none. A change to timeout, auth or reasoning-suppression must be made twice.
records.architectural_risk: Divergent behaviour between the chat path and the agent/dashboard path; reasoning tokens can leak to the UI on the Stack B path since it has no ThinkFilter equivalent (it only sets extra_body enable_thinking=False at router.py:163, the same flag llm.py:16-18 explicitly says cannot be trusted alone).

records.capability: Direct external-provider call bypassing the gateway (Azure OpenAI)
records.evidence: backend/orchestrator/router.py:84-89 `from openai import AsyncAzureOpenAI` / `AsyncAzureOpenAI(azure_endpoint=m["azure_endpoint"], api_key=m["api_key"], api_version=...)`; registry entry `MODELS["azure"]` router.py:58-67 with `"azure_endpoint": os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT", "https://nazo-openai.openai.azure.com")`; selector `dashboard_model()` router.py:70-75. LIVE in production config: .env:55 `DASHBOARD_LLM=azure`, .env:56 `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT=https://nazo-openai.openai.azure.com`, .env:57 `AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT=gpt-4.1`, .env:59 `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY=<set>`. Reached from backend/routes/dashboard.py:24 and backend/routes/agent_os.py:30 (`from backend.orchestrator.router import dashboard_model`) -> backend/dashboard/ask.py:198 / backend/dashboard/stream.py:97 (`"model_key": model_key`) -> graph.py:64 -> router.complete().
records.current_implementation: AsyncAzureOpenAI SDK client constructed in-process, cached in router._clients, called at router.py:166 `await _client(mk).chat.completions.create(timeout=90, **kwargs)`.
records.gap: This is the only call site in the repo that reaches a model provider without traversing LiteLLM. The Azure API key lives in the app process rather than the gateway, and these calls are invisible to any gateway-side rate limiting, key rotation or cost accounting.
records.architectural_risk: Provider credentials and egress bypass the single chokepoint the architecture is built around. Note router.py:161 also skips the enable_thinking suppression for provider=='azure', so the two paths differ in payload shape as well.

records.capability: Model profiles / in-code model registry
records.evidence: backend/orchestrator/router.py:35-48 `MODELS: dict[str, dict]` with exactly three static keys — `"gateway"`, `"gateway-fast"`, `"vision-vl"` — each carrying `caps` {tool_call, vision, ctx}, `tier`, `cost_in`, `cost_out`; a fourth key `"azure"` is added conditionally at router.py:57-67. Per-agent overrides are persisted: backend/db/models.py:109 `model_key: Mapped[str | None]`, backend/db/models.py:110 `fallback_models: Mapped[dict] = mapped_column(JSONB, server_default=text("'[]'::jsonb"))`, editable via backend/db/repo.py:175 `_EDITABLE_AGENT_FIELDS`.
records.current_implementation: Hardcoded dict + per-agent model_key/fallback_models columns consumed by router.plan() (router.py:105-110).
records.gap: No runtime-registrable model registry: `grep -rn model_config migrations/ backend/db/` returns nothing, and migrations/versions/ contains no model_configs table across all 7 revisions. project_overview/DEMO_PHASE_1_5_PLAN.md:105-109 specifies a DB-backed registry merging static keys with `model_configs` rows — that table was never created. Adding a model requires a code edit to router.py plus an out-of-repo LiteLLM edit.
records.architectural_risk: Model changes are code deploys, and the registry is split across two unsynchronised places (router.MODELS and the external LiteLLM model_list).

records.capability: Capability-based routing (tool-calling / vision / tier)
records.evidence: backend/orchestrator/router.py:95-97 `def _capable(key, need_tools, need_vision)` reading `MODELS[key]["caps"]`; backend/orchestrator/router.py:100-122 `def plan(agent, *, need_tools, need_vision, tier)` returning an ordered model_key list — vision branch :111-114, fast-tier branch :115-118, DEFAULT_CHAIN tail :119-121, guaranteed non-empty `return chain or ["gateway"]` :122. Vision demand is derived at backend/orchestrator/graph.py:64 `need_vision=has_image`.
records.current_implementation: Static caps dict + ordered-chain planner inside the second (router) stack only. backend/services/llm.py has no capability routing — callers pass `model=` explicitly.
records.gap: Capability metadata is asserted in code, never verified against the gateway. graph.py:51-55 documents that vision-vl is launched without --enable-auto-tool-choice, so `"tool_call": True` on the vision-vl entry (router.py:46) contradicts the deployment and is worked around by sending tools=None on image turns rather than by fixing the caps flag.
records.architectural_risk: caps can drift from what the served model actually supports; the vision-vl tool_call flag already has.

records.capability: Fallback chain on model failure
records.target_requirement: One fallback policy owned by the gateway
records.evidence: App-side: backend/orchestrator/router.py:50 `DEFAULT_CHAIN = ["gateway", "gateway-fast"]` and router.py:155-178 loop `for mk in chain:` ... `except Exception as e: last_err = e; ... continue` ending in `raise RuntimeError(f"all models failed (chain={chain}): {last_err}")`. Gateway-side: backend/services/llm.py:7 states the gateway is where "retries, fallbacks and cost accounting live"; backend/routes/observability_explorer.py:728 renders the edge `{"source": "litellm", "target": "azure", "label": "gpt-4.1 fallback"}`.
records.current_implementation: router chain fallback in-app; LiteLLM fallback out-of-repo; no fallback in services/llm.py.
records.gap: Two fallback mechanisms exist for the same failure. backend/services/llm.py implements none of its own (single httpx.post at :205, returns "" on failure at :215), so the chat path relies solely on unversioned LiteLLM config while the agent path relies solely on router.DEFAULT_CHAIN. Both `"gateway"` and `"gateway-fast"` resolve to LLM_BASE_URL with `"gateway-fast"` model defaulting to LLM_MODEL (router.py:41 `os.getenv("LLM_FAST_MODEL", LLM_MODEL)`), so with LLM_FAST_MODEL unset the fallback retries the identical model on the identical endpoint.
records.architectural_risk: LLM_FAST_MODEL is absent from .env and from config/settings.py, making the DEFAULT_CHAIN tail a no-op retry against the same model — the failure it is meant to survive will recur.

records.capability: Direct OpenAI SDK clients bypassing backend/services/llm.py
records.evidence: config/settings.py:41 states the rule: "Call sites must use backend/services/llm.py rather than these values directly." Violations: (1) tasks/intent.py:2 `from openai import OpenAI`, tasks/intent.py:6 `client = OpenAI(base_url=LLM_BASE_URL, api_key=LLM_API_KEY or "unset")`, invoked at tasks/intent.py:33 `client.chat.completions.create(model=LLM_MODEL, ...)`. (2) backend/main.py:5 `from openai import OpenAI, AsyncOpenAI`, backend/main.py:1283 `client = OpenAI(base_url=LLM_BASE_URL, ...)`, backend/main.py:1284 `async_client = AsyncOpenAI(base_url=LLM_BASE_URL, ...)`. (3) backend/orchestrator/router.py:91 `AsyncOpenAI(base_url=m["base_url"], api_key=...)`.
records.current_implementation: Three separate OpenAI-SDK clients constructed against LLM_BASE_URL outside the gateway module.
records.gap: These reach the correct host (LLM_BASE_URL) but skip the gateway module, so they get none of strip_think (llm.py:86), the typed error hierarchy (llm.py:44-64), NO_THINK injection (llm.py:166) or the shared keep-alive pool. tasks/intent.py:40-43 still carries llama.cpp-era assumptions ('llama.cpp's server enforces this via a grammar') for a stack that is now vLLM behind LiteLLM.
records.architectural_risk: tasks/intent.py is a live inference path with no <think> stripping — Qwen3 reasoning can land inside the JSON it then json.loads (intent.py:55), and the guard is only a markdown-fence strip (intent.py:48-53).

records.capability: Dead OpenAI client objects in backend/main.py
records.target_requirement: No provider SDK objects outside the gateway
records.evidence: backend/main.py:1283 `client = OpenAI(...)` and backend/main.py:1284 `async_client = AsyncOpenAI(...)` are never invoked: `grep -cE "(^|[^_a-zA-Z.])(client|async_client)\.(chat|completions|embeddings)" backend/main.py` returns 0. The other `client` references in that module are locally-scoped httpx clients — backend/main.py:481 `async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:` (used at :482) and backend/main.py:1668 `async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=1.5) as client:` (used at :1669) — which shadow the module-level names. No external importer exists: `grep -rn "backend\.main\.(client|async_client)"` returns nothing.
records.current_implementation: Constructed at import, never called.
records.gap: Two unused module-level provider clients are constructed at import time, and they are the sole reason backend/main.py:5 imports the OpenAI SDK.
records.architectural_risk: Low functional risk; they make backend/main.py appear to be a provider call site during audits and keep an SDK dependency alive for nothing.

records.capability: Embedding model access
records.evidence: Three independent fastembed loaders, none routed through any gateway: (1) backend/ingest.py:48 `from fastembed import TextEmbedding`, :62-66 `def get_embedder()` / `_embedder = TextEmbedding(model_name=EMBED_MODEL_NAME)`, used at :244 `list(get_embedder().embed(chunks))` and :333. (2) memory/long_term.py:35-37 `from fastembed import TextEmbedding` / `_embedder = TextEmbedding(model_name=EMBED_MODEL_NAME)`, used at :64. (3) backend/main.py:7 `from fastembed import TextEmbedding` and backend/main.py:1298 `embed_model = TextEmbedding(model_name="BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5")` — a HARDCODED literal that ignores config/settings.py:116 EMBED_MODEL_NAME.
records.current_implementation: In-process ONNX embedding via fastembed, loaded lazily in ingest/long_term and eagerly in main.
records.gap: Embeddings never traverse the Model Gateway; there is no `embed()` function in backend/services/llm.py. Instance (3) is additionally dead by its own admission — backend/main.py:1292-1295 states "nothing in this module reads `embed_model`" — yet it still loads a full model into RSS whenever LOAD_EMBED_MODEL is true (settings.py:128, default 'true'), costing the ~0.23 GB documented at settings.py:124.
records.architectural_risk: Setting EMBED_MODEL_NAME changes two of three loaders; backend/main.py:1298 keeps loading bge-small-en-v1.5 regardless, so a model change silently produces a mixed-dimension situation and wastes memory on a model nothing reads. EMBED_MODEL_NAME and EMBED_DIM are also undocumented in .env.example.

records.capability: Vision / image model routing (scanned-PDF OCR)
records.evidence: backend/ingest.py:140 `def _ocr_pdf_via_vision(path, max_pages=6)`; :153-154 `from backend.services import llm as _llm` / `from config.settings import LLM_VISION_MODEL as vl_model`; :166-172 `_llm.complete([{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", ...}, {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": data_url}}]}], model=vl_model, temperature=0, max_tokens=2048, timeout=120.0)`. Config: config/settings.py:47 `LLM_VISION_MODEL = os.getenv("LLM_VISION_MODEL", "qwen-vl")`, set in .env:4 `LLM_VISION_MODEL=qwen-vl`. Second vision route: backend/orchestrator/router.py:44-47 `"vision-vl"` entry with `caps.vision: True`, selected by plan() at router.py:111-114.
records.current_implementation: OCR path correctly calls _llm.complete with a data: URI image payload and an explicit model + extended timeout.
records.gap: Two vision entry points with different model resolution — ingest.py reads LLM_VISION_MODEL directly, router.py wraps it in the `vision-vl` key. Whether the `qwen-vl` alias is actually registered cannot be verified because the LiteLLM model_list is not in the repo.
records.architectural_risk: backend/orchestrator/graph.py:51-55 documents that the deployed vision-vl is launched without --enable-auto-tool-choice, so router.py:46 `"tool_call": True` overstates its capability.

records.capability: Dedicated KG extraction model route (long-deadline)
records.target_requirement: Per-workload model routing behind the gateway
records.evidence: config/settings.py:230-231 `KG_EXTRACT_MODEL = os.getenv("KG_EXTRACT_MODEL", "qwen-extract")` and `KG_EXTRACT_TIMEOUT = float(os.getenv("KG_EXTRACT_TIMEOUT", "300"))`; backend/knowledge_graph/extractor.py:31 imports both, :36-37 `EXTRACT_TIMEOUT = _CFG_TIMEOUT` / `EXTRACT_MODEL = _CFG_MODEL`, :245-247 `self._model = model or EXTRACT_MODEL`, :249-252 `model_name` property falling back to LLM_MODEL, and the call at :266-269 `_llm.complete(..., model=self._model, ...)` with `raise_on_error=True` (extractor.py:261-264 explains the rationale). Surfaced at backend/routes/observability.py:361-362 as `"extraction_model"` / `"extraction_timeout_s"`.
records.current_implementation: Separate LiteLLM alias with a 300s client deadline, invoked through backend/services/llm.py with typed-error propagation.
records.gap: KG_EXTRACT_MODEL is absent from both .env and .env.example, so production runs on the `qwen-extract` default whose existence in the LiteLLM model_list cannot be confirmed from the repo. extractor.py:34-36 notes the client deadline must not exceed the gateway's route timeout — that gateway-side value is unversioned.
records.architectural_risk: If the qwen-extract alias is missing, vLLM 404s (per backend/services/llm.py:12) and every KG extraction fails as LLMGatewayError.

records.capability: Speech models (Whisper STT / TTS) relative to the gateway
records.evidence: In-process, never gateway-routed: integrations/whisper_transcriber.py:15 `from faster_whisper import WhisperModel`, :37-46 `def get_model()` / `_model = WhisperModel(WHISPER_MODEL, device=device, compute_type=compute)`; integrations/tts.py:1 `from kokoro import KPipeline`. Consumers: backend/routes/voice.py:76, backend/main.py:1084, :3816, :3943, integrations/telegram_bot.py:18. Separate HTTP STT path bypassing the gateway module: backend/main.py:1043 `async def _stt_whispercpp(raw, filename)`, :1053-1054 `await get_llm_http().post(f"{WHISPER_CPP_URL}/inference", files=files, ...)` — reusing the httpx pool named `_llm_http` (backend/main.py:1322-1331) for a non-LLM call. Config: config/settings.py:106-108 WHISPER_MODEL/WHISPER_DEVICE/WHISPER_COMPUTE, :98 WHISPER_CPP_URL (default empty).
records.current_implementation: faster-whisper + Kokoro loaded in-process; optional whisper.cpp HTTP fast path gated on WHISPER_CPP_URL, which defaults to empty (settings.py:98).
records.gap: Speech models are a fourth inference channel entirely outside the Model Gateway, with their own model selection, device placement and failure handling. `get_llm_http()` is a duplicate of backend/services/llm.py:238 `get_client()` (identical Limits: max_keepalive_connections=8, keepalive_expiry=300.0) and its only caller is the STT POST at main.py:1053.
records.architectural_risk: GPU model lifecycle lives in the API process rather than behind a gateway; a misnamed shared HTTP pool (`_llm_http`) couples STT transport to LLM-transport tuning.

records.capability: Containerised STT/TTS services and their URL settings
records.target_requirement: Deployment matches the code's actual model topology
records.evidence: docker-compose.yml:14 `whisper_stt:` (image onerahmet/openai-whisper-asr-webservice, ports 5003:9000) and docker-compose.yml:22 `piper_tts:` (image ghcr.io/rhasspy/piper, port 5002). Matching config: config/settings.py:83 `TTS_URL = os.getenv("TTS_URL", "http://100.107.179.44:5002")`, :84 `STT_URL = os.getenv("STT_URL", "http://100.107.179.44:5003")`. Both are imported exactly once — backend/main.py:31 `from config.settings import TTS_URL, STT_URL` — and never referenced again; repo-wide `grep -rn "\bTTS_URL\b|\bSTT_URL\b" --include=*.py` returns only that import and the two definitions. backend/main.py:1677 confirms: "TTS / STT — now local Python modules (Kokoro / faster-whisper) rather...".
records.current_implementation: Orphaned compose services plus dead imports left over from the pre-in-process speech architecture.
records.gap: Two containers are declared and restart-always while nothing in the codebase can call them; two settings are imported to satisfy nothing.
records.architectural_risk: Ports 5002/5003 held by services no code path uses; an operator reading docker-compose.yml would conclude STT/TTS are remote when they run in-process.

records.capability: Model-gateway configuration centralisation (settings.py discipline)
records.target_requirement: All gateway config declared in config/settings.py
records.evidence: config/settings.py:243-248 states the rule explicitly (config must be "Declared HERE, not read with a bare os.getenv at the call site", citing prior bugs). Violations reading model config via bare os.getenv: backend/routes/observability.py:256 `vllm_url = os.getenv("VLLM_FAST_URL", "http://localhost:9002")`; backend/orchestrator/router.py:41 `os.getenv("LLM_FAST_MODEL", LLM_MODEL)`; router.py:56 `os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY", "")`; router.py:60-62 AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT / AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION / AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT; router.py:73 `os.getenv("DASHBOARD_LLM", "")`. Documentation drift: .env.example declares only LLM_BASE_URL (:12), LLM_MODEL (:13), LLM_API_KEY (:14), LLM_TIMEOUT (:15), WHISPER_MODEL (:134-136) — it omits LLM_VISION_MODEL, KG_EXTRACT_MODEL, KG_EXTRACT_TIMEOUT, LLM_FAST_MODEL, EMBED_MODEL_NAME, EMBED_DIM, VLLM_FAST_URL, DASHBOARD_LLM and every AZURE_OPENAI_* key, all of which are live in .env or in code.
records.current_implementation: Core LLM_* keys are centralised correctly; Azure, fast-model and vLLM-probe keys are not.
records.gap: Six model-routing env vars — including the one that switches an entire agent family onto a paid external provider (DASHBOARD_LLM) — are invisible in both config/settings.py and .env.example.
records.architectural_risk: The exact failure class settings.py:243-248 documents — a module reading os.getenv before config.settings is imported and silently seeing a default. VLLM_FAST_URL defaulting to localhost:9002 also makes the health card report a hardcoded port that no longer matches the deployment described in project_overview/DEMO_PHASE_1_5_PLAN.md:58.

records.capability: Automated tests for the gateway module
records.evidence: No test file targets backend/services/llm.py: `grep -rln -E "strip_think|ThinkFilter|services\.llm|build_payload|LLMTimeoutError|LLMGatewayError" tests/` returns only tests/test_knowledge_graph.py, and its single hit is a stub at tests/test_knowledge_graph.py:107 ("Stands in for backend.services.llm.complete."). No tests/test_llm*.py exists in the 35-file tests/ directory. The nearest live-gateway test, tests/test_radio_routing.py:27 `URL = LLM_BASE_URL.rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"`, builds raw urllib requests (:35,:56) that bypass the gateway module entirely and self-skips when the gateway is down (tests/test_radio_routing.py:42-43 `needs_model = pytest.mark.skipif(not _gateway_up(), ...)`).
records.current_implementation: No coverage; the only gateway-touching test requires a live gateway and skips silently otherwise.
records.gap: ThinkFilter's cross-chunk tag reassembly (llm.py:100-151), strip_think's truncated-block handling (llm.py:86-97), the _classify error mapping (llm.py:172-185) and build_payload's NO_THINK injection (llm.py:154-167) are all untested pure functions on the hot path.
records.architectural_risk: ThinkFilter is stateful streaming logic where a regression leaks raw <think> reasoning into user-visible output, and nothing would catch it in CI.

records.capability: Background job execution — what it uses today
records.evidence: APScheduler only. backend/main.py:13 `from apscheduler.schedulers.asyncio import AsyncIOScheduler`; backend/main.py:59 `scheduler = AsyncIOScheduler()` constructed with NO jobstore or executor argument (grep for `jobstore|JobStore|SQLAlchemyJobStore|configure(` across backend/, scheduler/, integrations/ returns zero hits) — i.e. the default in-memory MemoryJobStore. Started at backend/main.py:769 `scheduler.start()`, stopped at :800 `scheduler.shutdown()`. 18 `add_job` call sites. Registered job ids: index_sweep (backend/storage/indexing.py:391), user_directory_refresh (main.py:610), fire_reminders (:630), prune_embeds (:647), refresh_channel_directory (:657), rag_ingest (:700), agent_inbox_poll (:754), session_cleanup (:762), plus per-user digest_{uid}, morning_brief_{uid}, eod_{uid}, due_tasks_{uid}, memory_extract_{uid} and per-schedule user_schedule_{id} (:527, :537). Unnamed jobs: poll_inbox 30 s (:624), check_upcoming_meetings 5 min (:632), _premeeting_sweep (:693). Whole subsystem gated by RUN_BACKGROUND (config/settings.py:153, checked at main.py:615-623). apscheduler 3.11.2 is the installed version.
records.gap: Jobs live only in process memory; a restart loses every scheduled job and they are re-registered from scratch at lifespan startup. There is no cross-process job ownership, no distributed lock, and `max_instances=1, coalesce=True` only guards within one process.
records.architectural_risk: backend/main.py:53-58 records that a lambda passed to add_job was dispatched to a worker THREAD and raised "RuntimeError: no running event loop" 223 times, silently killing eight job types; the fix was functools.partial over a coroutine function. This failure mode is invisible — a broken job simply never runs.

records.capability: Durability of background work (queue substitute)
records.evidence: Work is re-derived from database rows, deliberately. backend/storage/indexing.py:17-29 states verbatim: "Why no queue... the deployment is ONE uvicorn process. A broker would add a second source of truth about what needs indexing, which can disagree with the row that already records it. So: an in-process asyncio task for latency, and an APScheduler sweep over Postgres for durability... The architectural trigger to revisit... a SECOND uvicorn worker, multiple replicas, a measured backlog, or a need for cross-process job ownership." Implemented by `register_sweep()` (indexing.py:375-396, job id "index_sweep", 2 min) wired at backend/main.py:850-851; state machine stored/processing/indexed/failed with MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 (:51), STALE_PROCESSING_AFTER=15 min (:55), RETRY_BACKOFF (1 m, 5 m, 30 m) (:56), SWEEP_BATCH=10 (:57). User schedules are likewise reloaded on boot: `load_all_active_schedules()` from scheduler/schedule_manager.py, iterated at backend/main.py:746-752.
records.gap: This is a correct single-process design, not a gap. It provides at-least-once redelivery and bounded retry without a broker. It has no dead-letter destination — exhausted documents simply remain `failed` for a human (indexing.py:49-51).
records.architectural_risk: backend/storage/indexing.py:28-29: "The in-process duplicate guard below is correct for one process and is NOT sufficient for several; that is the first thing that breaks on worker #2." The guard is `_active: dict[str, asyncio.Task]` at :63. backend/main.py:322 `_briefed_events: set = set()` is the same pattern for meeting-brief dedup and has the same limitation.

The same routers expose `/observability/graph`, `/observability/qdrant`, `/observability/documents` and Neo4j entity lookups (observability_explorer.py:271, :300, :466, :800) with no tenant scoping.
records.architectural_risk: Confidentiality break across every user in the deployment.

records.capability: Tenant isolation (org scoping)
records.target_requirement: org_id as a mandatory predicate injected by the PolicyInterface / repo layer, and an org-partitioned shared corpus.
records.evidence: Schema is org-aware: backend/db/models.py:40 `class Organization` (`slug` unique), and `org_id = fk("organizations.id", index=True)` on users, agents, agent_permissions, agent_runs, approvals, tasks, documents, document_chunks, email_threads, chat_sessions and more. Org is derived per email domain at backend/db/repo.py:88-95 (`org_slug = domain or DEFAULT_ORG_SLUG`, DEFAULT_ORG_SLUG="meerana" at repo.py:37). But NO query in backend/db/repo.py filters on org_id — every read is user-scoped only: repo.py:217 `select(M.Task).where(M.Task.user_id == user_id, ...)`, repo.py:282 `select(M.Approval).where(M.Approval.user_id == user_id)`, repo.py:324 opportunities, repo.py:348 interactions, repo.py:393 chat sessions. Vector store: backend/ingest.py:326 `must = [FieldCondition(key="user_id", match=MatchAny(any=allowed))]` where `allowed = [ORG_OWNER] if owner is None else [owner, ORG_OWNER]` (ingest.py:325); `org_id` IS written into the payload (ingest.py:264) but appears in no `FieldCondition` anywhere (grep over backend/). The `ORG_OWNER = "__org__"` sentinel (ingest.py:47) is a single global bucket shared by all organizations. The one org-aware authorization check in the codebase is backend/storage/documents.py:245 `if requester_org_id is not None and str(requester_org_id) != owner_org`. Per-user memory is physically isolated: memory/long_term.py:51 `collection_name = f"{COLLECTION_PREFIX}{user_id}"` with fail-closed memory/long_term.py:17 `_require_uid`.
records.current_implementation: org_id columns + per-user filtering; one org check in the storage module.
records.gap: Isolation is de facto per-user, not per-tenant. org_id is written everywhere and used as an authorization predicate in exactly one function. The shared `__org__` RAG corpus is not partitioned by organization, so a second tenant's users would see the first tenant's shared documents.
records.architectural_risk: The multi-tenant story is schema-deep but not query-deep; it holds today only because one organization is live.

records.capability: Secrets management and encryption at rest
records.target_requirement: Central secret store + declared key rotation; encrypt/classify the remaining credential fields.
records.evidence: backend/services/token_crypto.py implements Fernet AEAD with an `enc::` idempotence prefix (token_crypto.py:20-21 `_PREFIX`, `SENSITIVE = ("access_token", "refresh_token")`), key resolution `TOKEN_ENC_KEY` env → .env file read → auto-generated `data_vault/.token_enc_key` chmod 600 (token_crypto.py:30-56), and `enc_row`/`dec_row` helpers. One-shot migration at migrate_encrypt_tokens.py (with a round-trip assertion, line 49) and manual rotation at rekey_tokens.py (decrypts with keyfile key, re-encrypts with the .env key, unlinks the keyfile, line 40). .gitignore explicitly closes timestamped-backup leaks (`\.env.*`, `*.bak.*`, `data_vault/*.json.bak*`) with a comment naming the leaked files.
records.current_implementation: Application-level Fernet for OAuth tokens; everything else is plaintext env.
records.gap: Only two fields are encrypted — `SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY`, `INTERNAL_API_TOKEN`, `M365_CLIENT_SECRET`, `NEO4J_PASSWORD` and DB URLs live in plaintext .env with no vault/KMS. No automated rotation (rekey_tokens.py is a hand-run repair script). Governance env keys are undocumented in .env.example (163 lines, no `INTERNAL_API_TOKEN`, `ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS`, `RATE_LIMIT_*`, `AGANETI_DATA_BACKEND`, `DEV_AUTH_BYPASS` entries). `DASHBOARD_ORIGINS` and `AUTONOMY_LEVEL` are absent from the live .env, so backend/main.py:960 falls back to `os.getenv("DASHBOARD_ORIGINS", "*")` → `allow_origins=["*"]` with `allow_headers=["*"]` (main.py:961-967). A tracked file carries live project config: frontend/.env.production (`VITE_SUPABASE_URL`, `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`) is in `git ls-files`.
records.architectural_risk: Medium; the highest-value secrets (OAuth tokens) are covered, the rest are not.

records.capability: Audit trail
records.target_requirement: Every PolicyInterface decision and every identity/permission mutation emits an immutable event.
records.evidence: backend/db/models.py:188 `class Event` / `events` with `ts` (indexed), `org_id`, `user_id`, `agent_id`, `run_id`, `kind`, `name`, `success`, `duration_ms`, `cost_micros`, `meta` JSONB. Writer: backend/db/repo.py:300-305 `log_event`, plus backend/events.py:79. Emitted for approvals (backend/orchestrator/store.py:215 `kind="approval"`), delegations (backend/delegation.py:172, :210, :227), and chart lifecycle (backend/dashboard/tools.py:188 `_audit`, :281 `CHART_SAVED`, :296 `CHART_DELETED`). Request-level tracing exists separately via `_TraceASGIMiddleware` (backend/main.py:905) emitting `x-trace-id`.
records.current_implementation: An application events spine used opportunistically by three subsystems.
records.gap: No audit event for security-relevant identity actions: authentication success/failure (backend/auth/enforce.py logs 401/403 to the logger only, enforce.py:142, :162), permission grant/revoke (backend/db/repo.py:164 and :190 write no event), provider connect/disconnect (backend/routes/provider_auth.py logs only, :283), or role/status changes. `Event` has no append-only constraint, no hash chain, and no retention policy. The sqlite approval backend writes no event at all (backend/orchestrator/store.py:109).
records.architectural_risk: Medium: the workflow that most needs an audit trail (approvals) has one; identity and permission changes do not.

records.capability: Rate limiting / abuse control
records.target_requirement: Principal-scoped quotas evaluated by the PolicyInterface, backed by a shared store when horizontal scaling arrives.
records.evidence: backend/ratelimit.py:35 `class RateLimitMiddleware` (pure ASGI, documented at ratelimit.py:3-6 as deliberately not BaseHTTPMiddleware so SSE streams survive), mounted at backend/main.py:885-886 inside auth. Sliding window in `_buckets: dict[str, deque]` (ratelimit.py:28) keyed `f"{ip}:{klass}"` (ratelimit.py:59), IP from `x-forwarded-for` else socket peer (ratelimit.py:54-55). Tighter bucket for `_CHAT_PREFIXES` (ratelimit.py:23) via `RATE_LIMIT_CHAT_MAX` (default 20) vs `RATE_LIMIT_MAX` (default 120), window `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW` (default 60). Returns 429 with `retry-after`, `x-ratelimit-limit`, `x-ratelimit-window` (ratelimit.py:69-74). Loopback exempt (ratelimit.py:50).
records.current_implementation: Single-instance in-memory sliding window by client IP.
records.gap: State is in-process only — no shared store (no redis/memcached in requirements.txt; docker-compose.yml declares only qdrant, whisper_stt, piper_tts), so limits are per-worker and reset on restart. Keyed by IP, not by authenticated principal or org, so a shared NAT egress shares one bucket and one compromised account is not individually throttled. No per-user quota or cost cap despite `AgentRun.cost_micros` (backend/db/models.py:145) being recorded.
records.architectural_risk: Low today (single instance); blocks horizontal scaling.

records.capability: Data classification and sensitivity-based filtering
records.target_requirement: A real classification vocabulary consumed as a PolicyInterface attribute and pushed into the retrieval filter.
records.evidence: Columns exist: backend/db/models.py:325 and :343 `sensitivity: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, server_default=text("'internal'"))` on `documents` and `document_chunks`; migrations/versions/20260708_2100_30811c8467d2_rag_lineage_tables.py:31 and :107 create them. Vocabulary is only two values, derived from storage scope: backend/storage/documents.py:56 `SENSITIVITY = {SCOPE_ORG: "internal", SCOPE_PRIVATE: "private"}`, with scope constants at backend/storage/object_store.py:61-62. Qdrant indexes the field (backend/ingest.py:93 `("sensitivity", "keyword")`) and stores it per point (ingest.py:266) and returns it per hit (ingest.py:349). Object-key hardening is real: object_store.py:58 `_KEY_RE`, :89 `validate_key`, :104 `key_is_owned_by`, used as a second check at documents.py:251.
records.current_implementation: A two-value label mirroring storage scope, indexed but never queried.
records.gap: `sensitivity` is never used as a filter: backend/ingest.py:326-330 builds `must` from `user_id`, `source_type` and `timestamp` only. No classifier assigns it — it is a constant defaulted from scope. No confidential/restricted tier, no PII or DLP detection anywhere (the only redaction in the tree is backend/storage/client.py:49 `_redact`, which strips S3 secret keys from exception strings). Prompt-injection defense is instruction-only (backend/main.py:2121-2125 SECURITY block) with no runtime detector.
records.architectural_risk: Retrieval cannot express "this user may not see restricted content" — only "this user owns it or it is shared".

records.capability: Structured application logging with per-request trace IDs
records.target_requirement: Machine-parseable logs correlatable to persisted telemetry

records.current_implementation: Python stdlib logging, one rotating text file plus stdout, trace id carried in a ContextVar. 76 module loggers created via logging.getLogger() across backend/.
records.gap: Log lines are free-text, not JSON — every downstream consumer has to regex them (see backend/routes/observability.py:729 _ACTIVITY_PATTERNS and backend/routes/observability_explorer.py:66 _STAGE_RE). The trace id is never written into any DB row, so a log line cannot be joined to an events/chat_messages record.
records.architectural_risk: Correlating a user-reported failure to its telemetry requires grepping a 5 MB rotating file; after ~4 rotations the evidence is gone.

records.capability: Event-write path (two independent implementations)
records.evidence: Writer A: backend/events.py:57 def log_event(kind,*,user_id,...) — synchronous, opens its own session via `from backend.db import models as M, sync as _s` and `with _s.session() as ses: ses.add(M.Event(...)); ses.commit()` (events.py:65-83), with a SQLite fallback branch (events.py:86-94). Writer B: backend/db/repo.py:299 async def log_event(s: AsyncSession, *, kind, name, org_id, user_id, agent_id, run_id, success, duration_ms, cost_micros, meta) — `s.add(M.Event(...))` (repo.py:304), no fallback, caller-supplied session. Both target the same M.Event/`events` table. Writer B has exactly one caller: backend/orchestrator/store.py:215 `await repo.log_event(s, kind="approval", ...)`.
records.current_implementation: Sync path used by 13 call sites; async path used by 1.
records.gap: The two writers differ in behaviour, not just style: A resolves the external user id to an internal UUID (events.py:69 `_s.resolve_user`) and lifts cost_micros out of meta (events.py:81); B requires pre-resolved UUIDs and takes run_id/org_id explicitly, which A cannot set at all except agent_uuid via meta (events.py:73-78). Neither is documented as canonical.
records.architectural_risk: Any new telemetry field must be added twice or it silently exists on only some events; the sync writer opening its own session inside an async request path blocks the event loop.

Cost table: router.py:39,43,47 set "cost_in": 0, "cost_out": 0 for gateway, gateway-fast and vision-vl; router.py:66 sets cost_in 2000 / cost_out 8000 for the azure entry only. Aggregated by backend/events.py:289-290 SUM(...tokens_in), SUM(...tokens_out), SUM(COALESCE(cost_micros,0)). The primary chat path does NOT use this: backend/main.py:1382 call_llm_tools and :1412 call_llm_tools_stream call `_llm.acomplete_raw` (backend/services/llm.py), and a grep of backend/services/llm.py finds no usage/token/cost extraction and no events call — its only telemetry is log.warning on failure (llm.py:212, 267, 290).

records.capability: Qdrant corporate RAG isolation (collection + search filter)
records.target_requirement: RAG results never cross an organization

records.capability: Consistency of the Qdrant ACL identifier across ingest paths
records.evidence: backend/storage/indexing.py:160 `owner = str(row["user_id"])`, :192 `ingest_file(client, tmp, owner, org_id=str(row["org_id"])...)`; backend/main.py:1202 `ingest_file(c, t, user_id, org_id=org_id, source_type="file")`; backend/context/providers/corporate.py:36-37 `search_corporate, request.message, self.top_k, request.user_id`; backend/main.py:1123-1126 comment naming the two ids explicitly

records.capability: Neo4j knowledge-graph tenant isolation (labels/properties/queries)
records.target_requirement: Graph retrieval never returns another tenant's facts
records.evidence: config/settings.py:59 `NEO4J_DATABASE`; backend/knowledge_graph/client.py:131-133 `def database()`; backend/knowledge_graph/queries.py:152 `BASE_LABEL = "Entity"`, :193 `MERGE (n:Entity {id: row.id})`, :291-292 expansion query, :231-233 lookup by name; backend/knowledge_graph/provenance.py:33 `LIST_FIELDS` includes "user_ids"; backend/knowledge_graph/retrieval/retriever.py:52 `def expand(self, seed_ids, depth=1, rel_types=None)`; backend/context/providers/graph.py:72-73 `api.retrieve, request.message, depth=self.depth, top_k=self.top_k`
records.current_implementation: One global graph in one database. `NEO4J_DATABASE = os.getenv("NEO4J_DATABASE", "neo4j")` and `def database()` returns it for every session. All nodes share `BASE_LABEL = "Entity"` and are merged purely on id: `MERGE (n:Entity {id: row.id})`. Expansion, lookup, fulltext and edge queries carry no owner predicate (`MATCH (a:Entity {id: seed_id})-[r]-(b:Entity) WHERE NOT b.id IN $visited`). Provenance accumulates `user_ids` as an array property (LIST_FIELDS) but retriever.py:178 explicitly excludes it from the filterable set, and `GraphRetriever.expand(seed_ids, depth, rel_types)` takes no user or org argument. `GraphProvider.collect` calls `api.retrieve(request.message, depth=..., top_k=...)` — the request's user_id is never passed.
records.gap: Entities extracted from one organization's documents and conversations are merged into the same `:Entity` nodes every other organization traverses. There is no label, property or database boundary to filter on — `user_ids` is recorded for provenance display only.
records.architectural_risk: The frozen GraphRAG production config (resolver 0.82, depth 1, graph_top_k 8, hop_decay 0.55, fusion 0.60, max_nodes 100) is tuned against this single merged graph. Partitioning by tenant — whether by property predicate, label, or database-per-tenant — changes node degree and neighbourhood density, so the frozen numbers cannot be assumed to carry over.

records.capability: Object storage isolation (key prefixes / bucket ACL)
records.evidence: backend/storage/object_store.py:58 `_KEY_RE`, :69-86 `build_key`, :89-101 `validate_key`, :104-115 `key_is_owned_by`, :155-156 `_path`; config/settings.py:258 `SEAWEEDFS_BUCKET_NAME`; backend/storage/documents.py:245 `if requester_org_id is not None and ...`; grep for `fetch_document` finds no route caller

Filenames never enter a key (`safe_basename`). But all prefixes live in ONE bucket reached with ONE S3 identity: `SEAWEEDFS_BUCKET_NAME = os.getenv("SEAWEEDFS_BUCKET_NAME", "agentic-ai")`, `self._path(key) -> f"/{self._bucket}/{validate_key(key)}"`. records.gap: Prefix separation is defence in depth, not enforcement — one credential can read every prefix. The one org-aware ACL function in the codebase is unreachable from HTTP, and it fails open when the org is unknown, which is the normal case since no caller can obtain an org (no TenantContext).
records.architectural_risk: When a download route is finally wired up, the `requester_org_id is not None` shape will silently authorize cross-org reads for every caller that cannot supply an org — which today is every caller.

records.capability: Tenant dimension in logs, metrics, events and background jobs
records.target_requirement: Every log line, metric and job carries and respects a tenant id

records.current_implementation: Postgres `events` HAS org_id (`org_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None]`, indexed, no FK) and `events.log_event` populates it by resolving the user. records.gap: Telemetry cannot be segmented or exported per tenant, and one analytics path (email triage) is an outright cross-user data leak: senders and subjects from any mailbox are surfaced to any user asking for `top_contacts`.
records.architectural_risk: logs/email_log.json is capped at the last 50 entries globally, so it also silently loses one user's history when another is active — a correctness bug on top of the leak.

The SHA-256 prefixes exist only inside hand-written manifests (graphrag_quality_gate_final_v1_manifest.json:6-10) and in prose at docs/evaluation/graphrag_quality_gate_final_v1.md:201. GoldenCase.from_dict (backend/evals/dataset.py:79-81) filters to `known = {f for f in cls.__slots__}`, so `dataset_version`, `correction_version` and `_correction` are silently dropped and never reach the loader or the report.
records.current_implementation: The freeze is documentary. The only executable guard on the dataset is the case-count assertion at tests/test_eval_scoring.py:102 plus the invariant tests around it — nothing verifies file content hashes at run time, and no report records which dataset version produced it (render_report only emits `dataset_name`, report.py:78-79).
records.gap: A single-character edit to any expectation in a case file changes every metric with no signal anywhere. The `--baseline` regression check would attribute the shift to the system under test. Silent-drop in from_dict compounds this: a mistyped field name (e.g. `expected_graph_node`) vanishes without error, turning a scored expectation into an unscored one.
records.architectural_risk: Every published number becomes non-attributable to a dataset state. This is the failure mode the manifests were written to prevent, but nothing connects them to a run.

records.capability: Evaluation harness — pipeline runner, metrics, scoring, reporting
records.evidence: backend/evals/ contains 8 modules: dataset.py, runner.py (18KB), metrics.py, scoring.py (16KB), benchmark.py, report.py, visualizer.py, fixture.py, plus the CLI run_evals.py:105 `async def main()`. Public API declared in backend/evals/__init__.py `__all__`. Runner stages are enumerated in runner.py:4-13 (resolve_only → retrieve → ContextBuilder.build_context → HybridContextFusion → WeightedRanker → ContextCompressor → ContextBudget → build_sections → optional LiteLLM answer), each timed by StageTiming (runner.py:44-74) and captured in RunTrace (runner.py:77-186). Scoring produces CaseScore/AggregateScore with six metric families declared at scoring.py:275-283 `_FAMILY_FIELDS` (entity_resolution, graph, qdrant, fusion, ranking, answer). run_evals.py exposes --seed/--teardown/--tags/--ids/--sweep/--tune-weights/--with-answers/--baseline/--save-baseline/--min-score/--report and documents exit codes at run_evals.py:15.
records.current_implementation: Stage-level, optional-metric design: an unstated expectation scores None rather than 0 (scoring.py:4-8), so the headline is not a measure of dataset completeness. Read-only by construction — backend/evals/__init__.py states nothing mutates Neo4j/Qdrant/Postgres, and fixture.py:9-10 is the single writer, gated behind `--seed`, tagged `source="eval-fixture"` and removed by the same tag (fixture.py:86-101). benchmark.py adds a fusion-threshold sweep (DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS 0.40-0.95, benchmark.py:33) and coordinate-descent ranking-weight search (rationale at benchmark.py:10-15).
records.gap: Scope. Every stage, metric and case file targets the retrieval/context pipeline. There is no runner stage, trace field or metric family for tool invocation, agent delegation, connector health, or policy decisions — RunTrace has no field for a tool call or an action outcome.
records.architectural_risk: The harness is the natural home for non-GraphRAG evaluation, but extending RunTrace/CaseScore for agent trajectories is a schema change to a structure that 43 tests and 41 artifacts depend on. Extension needs to be additive-only.
dependencies: backend.context (ContextBuilder, build_sections, fusion, ranking, compression, budget)

records.capability: Regression gate — saved baseline and drift detection
records.evidence: run_evals.py:36-37 `REPORT_DIR = .../reports/evals`, `BASELINE = REPORT_DIR / "baseline.json"`; run_evals.py:43 `REGRESSION_TOLERANCE = 0.02`; compare_baseline at run_evals.py:87-102 sets exit code 1 on a drop beyond tolerance. The on-disk baseline reports/evals/baseline.json holds `"overall": 0.6985` with families entity_resolution 0.7028 / graph 0.5162 / qdrant 0.2727 / fusion 0.9473 / ranking 0.6796 / answer 0.5639, file mtime 2026-08-05 16:08. The frozen v3.1 headline is 0.5867 (docs/evaluation/graphrag_quality_gate_final_v1.md:39). The newest saved report reports/evals/report_final.html is dated 2026-08-08 and states "116 case" — the dataset became 174 cases on 2026-08-09 (backend/evals/cases/discrimination.json mtime). .gitignore:65 ignores `reports/`; `git ls-files reports` returns only email_digest.py, pdf_generator.py and two templates — no eval report or baseline is tracked.
records.current_implementation: A single-file, machine-local baseline compared with a ±2pp tolerance on `overall` plus each family, with no record of which dataset, commit or configuration produced it (baseline.json stores only overall/families/totals/latency).
records.gap: Running `python run_evals.py --baseline` today compares a 174-case v3.1 run (≈0.5867) against a 116-case v2-era baseline (0.6985) and reports an ~11pp REGRESSION plus per-family regressions that reflect a dataset change, not a system change. Because the baseline is gitignored, no shared or CI-visible baseline exists at all.
records.architectural_risk: The gate is worse than absent: it produces confident false alarms, which trains people to pass --min-score 0 or skip the flag. It also has no notion of dataset identity, so it can never distinguish 'the system got worse' from 'the ground truth moved'.
records.recommended_phase: Phase 1 — re-baseline against v3.1 and version the baseline

records.capability: Tool-calling / tool-selection evaluation
records.evidence: evals/tool_calling_eval.py — 23-entry `GOLDEN` list (lines 44-68), `THRESHOLD = 0.85` (line 27), `PRIMARY_TOOLS = list(templates.PRIMARY_TOOLS)` and `SCHEMAS = registry.openai_schemas(PRIMARY_TOOLS)` (lines 31-32), driving the live router via `router.complete` in `_first_tool` (line 71-76) and returning exit 1 below threshold (line 127). Optional `--judge` path scores no-tool replies 1-5 via a second LLM call (`_judge`, line 83-92). Dependencies verified present: backend/orchestrator/templates.py:44-47 PRIMARY_TOOLS (18 tools), backend/orchestrator/registry.py:60 `def openai_schemas`, backend/orchestrator/router.py:147 `async def complete`, backend/orchestrator/registry.py:232 `register(Tool("list_emails"…`. A historical result is recorded in project_overview/NEXT_ROADMAP.md:26 "eval 95-100% / 22 cases (threshold 85%)".
records.current_implementation: Side-effect-free tool-CHOICE inspection against the real primary-agent schema set, with a release-gating exit code and an optional LLM-judge for the no-tool cases.
records.gap: Four gaps. (1) Selection only — `_first_tool` returns `tcs[0]["function"]["name"]` and never inspects arguments, so wrong-argument calls score as passes. (3) No persisted artifact — output is stdout only; there is no counterpart to reports/evals/report.json, so no trend, no baseline, no regression detection. records.architectural_risk: The one non-GraphRAG eval that exists produces no durable evidence and reuses none of backend/evals (no metrics.py, no scoring.py, no report.py). Its 0.85 threshold is unenforced by anything.

Every client is built without credentials: config/settings.py:50 `QDRANT_URL = os.getenv("QDRANT_URL", "http://100.107.179.44:6333")` and no QDRANT_API_KEY symbol exists; constructors at backend/ingest.py:71, memory/long_term.py:53,121,170, backend/main.py:1285, backend/routes/observability.py:138, backend/routes/observability_explorer.py:480 all pass `url=` only. backend/routes/observability_explorer.py:482-491 `for meta in c.get_collections().collections:` returns every collection name, point count and vector config to any authenticated caller.
records.gap: Domain A rated per-user Qdrant memory 'EXISTS / P3 / risk: None — strictly stronger than per-org'. Physical collection-per-user is only stronger if the instance is a trust boundary. It is not: it is keyless, network-reachable, and shared with an unrelated video-indexing application (matching the known Redis DB-0 sharing on the same host). Any process that can reach :6333 can read `corporate_memory` and all 13 user memory collections, and this app leaks the other application's collection inventory through /observability/qdrant. A's 'do not replace this with a single collection + payload filter — that would be a downgrade' is right about the shape and silent about the substrate.
records.architectural_risk: The strongest isolation claim in the tenancy domain rests on an unauthenticated multi-tenant-by-accident datastore.

records.capability: Guardrails 'comms' policy is not merely unenforced — it is misreported by the policy API while a real side effect fires
records.target_requirement: Outbound actions gated; policy API reflects behaviour
records.evidence: backend/tools.py:955-958 `from backend.guardrails import decide` / `if decide(name) == "deny": return ...` with the inline comment '(comms actions are still safe-by-design — draft_email queues a draft, it never sends)'. backend/guardrails.py:37 `"draft_email": "comms", # produces a draft in the approval queue, never sends`, :38 `"schedule_meeting": "comms"`, :73-74 `if cat == "comms": return "auto" if AUTONOMY_LEVEL == "autonomous" else "approval"` (default AUTONOMY_LEVEL='standard', guardrails.py:21 — absent from .env, so the default is live), :83 policy_snapshot note 'comms actions always create a draft for the user to send'. But backend/tools.py:1258-1286 `if name == "schedule_meeting":` … :1284 `created, err = _provider_call(mailbox.create_event(user_id, title, start, end, attendees=attendees))` returning 'Scheduled **{title}** for {start}.' — an immediate write to the user's real provider calendar.
records.gap: Domain C rated this PARTIAL ('a real, tested policy layer... bound to the legacy lane') and Domain F correctly noted the 'approval' verdict is discarded. Neither recorded that the policy's own documentation is false and is served over HTTP: GET /guardrails returns policy_snapshot() asserting comms always drafts, while the comms tool `schedule_meeting` performs an irreversible external write with the approval verdict computed and dropped. Status should be WRONG_ARCHITECTURE with a note that the misreporting is itself the hazard — a reviewer reading guardrails.py:83 or the /guardrails response concludes the gate holds.
records.architectural_risk: The only policy engine on the lane the shipped UI streams both fails open on 'approval' and publishes a claim that it does not.

records.capability: Domain A over-claims the /observability_explorer/pipeline leak; and under-cites the surface that is genuinely exposed

"user_1" used to be one, and it stopped naming a real account when identity moved to Supabase subs'. LIMIT 50`; mounted bare at backend/main.py:840.

records.capability: STATUS ERROR — agent_runs carries three different statuses across three domains from identical evidence
records.evidence: I verified the underlying fact: `grep -rn "create_run\|save_run_state\|finish_run" --include=*.py .` (excluding .venv/__pycache__) returns exactly three lines, all definitions — backend/db/repo.py:240, :251, :255. Zero callers. records.gap: A table with a full schema, a genesis migration, three unused helpers and no reader is a MISSING capability with pre-built scaffolding — not PARTIAL. PARTIAL reads as 'works for some cases', which is false; nothing writes a run row in any code path. The three domains must be reconciled to one record and one status, or the matrix contains a contradiction on a P0/P1 item.
records.architectural_risk: A reader taking PARTIAL at face value will look for the partial implementation and find nothing.

records.capability: MISSED SURFACE — rate limiting exists and is the only gateway-level policy enforcement point in the process
records.evidence: backend/ratelimit.py:1 'Basic in-memory rate limiting (Phase 0, Item 6) — pure ASGI', implemented as pure ASGI specifically so it does not buffer SSE (:3-6); `_WINDOW = os.getenv("RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW","60")` (:20), `_DEFAULT_MAX` 120 (:21), `_CHAT_MAX` 20 (:22), `_CHAT_PREFIXES = ("/chat", "/agent/chat", "/stt", "/tts", "/transcribe", "/meeting/transcribe", "/report/generate", "/ingest")` (:24), `_buckets: dict[str, deque]` (:29), emits x-ratelimit-limit / x-ratelimit-window headers (:72-73). Mounted at backend/main.py:885 `from backend.ratelimit import RateLimitMiddleware`.
records.gap: Absent from every finding provided (domains A-F), including B's model-gateway inventory and A's governance/permissions record. It matters twice over: it is the only place in the process where a request is refused on policy grounds, and it keys on client IP with a process-local dict — so it is neither per-user nor per-tenant, cannot express a tenant quota, and resets on restart. Any 'gateways enforce policy' target needs this recorded as the existing seam rather than rebuilt.
records.architectural_risk: A second rate limiter will be written because the first one was not inventoried; and an IP-keyed limiter behind a Tailscale/VM proxy shares one bucket across all users on that hop.

records.capability: Host secret handling — live credentials in a plaintext .env loaded wholesale by systemd, plus a superseded copy retained
records.evidence: deploy/aganeti-api.service:11 `EnvironmentFile=/home/matrix/aganetiAi/.env`; that file (86 lines, keys read without values) carries AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY (:59), SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY (:37), INTERNAL_API_TOKEN (:38), TOKEN_ENC_KEY (:44), DABS_CORESHARE_PASSWORD (:53), M365_CLIENT_SECRET (:20), GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET (:30), TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (:13), APP_PASSWORD (:9), SEAWEEDFS_SECRET_KEY (:77), NEO4J_PASSWORD (:67). A superseded copy persists on disk: `.env.bak.pre-litellm` (2,515 B, Jul 31), which .gitignore:38-41 describes as carrying 'client secrets + DB passwords', alongside data_vault/provider_connections.json.bak.20260806 ('OAuth access/refresh tokens'). Git hygiene itself is correct — .gitignore:1-3 covers .env / credentials.json / tokens/ and :42-44 covers the backup suffixes; `git ls-files` shows no secret-bearing file.
records.gap: Domain B recorded only that AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY is 'populated' as proof the bypass is live. No finding records that there is no secret manager, that the systemd unit injects the entire secret set into one process, or that superseded secret files (including OAuth refresh tokens) are retained on the host after rotation. TOKEN_ENC_KEY sitting in the same file as the ciphertext store's host config also means the Fernet-at-rest layer (backend/services/token_crypto.py) protects against database theft only, not host access — a caveat the 'keep' list for that layer should state.
records.architectural_risk: Encryption-at-rest presented as a strength while its key ships in the same file as the data's connection string.
